question: How big is a page and why does that matter?

beats.speaker: interviewer
beats.line: How big is a page and why does that matter?

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Linux defaults to four kilobyte pages, though transparent hugepages promote regions to two megabytes automatically under memory pressure.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Intel processors since Haswell also support one gigabyte pages, configured through the hugetlbfs pseudo filesystem at boot time.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Benchmarks from Google showed roughly fifteen percent throughput gains on database workloads after enabling hugepages across their fleet.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: So administrators tune the value per workload rather than accepting the kernel default configuration blindly.
